qualitative_rules.rule: Pain sections are second-person statements, not diagnostic questions. Questions may appear inside solutions. HARD as a prohibition in the guide, but classifying a question as diagnostic is judgment: the validator flags candidate question sentences and the reviewer confirms.
qualitative_rules.source: Section 2 lesson; production rules (the rule governs even where the historical challenge screenshots use questions)

qualitative_rules.rule: The Section 5 body opens with 'That is the reason why', 'That is why', or a natural equivalent. The two named forms are mechanically checkable; a natural equivalent is an either/or judgment the reviewer confirms.
Exactly three pains and three matched solutions; each solution answers its own preceding pain with a distinct mechanism; the three pains are genuinely distinct, not three versions of one pressure.
Each persona entry identifies a relevant person AND the need or desired outcome (connected via pain OR desire; both routes are valid and may mix across entries). A job title alone fails.
Inclusions are concrete, each with an appealing title and an explanation of immediate use, and only inclusions from the client brief.
Three distinct benefits; solutions, the inclusion list, and the benefits remain distinct from each other; a paragraph cannot merely be copied into all three locations.
qualitative_rules.source: Sequence and jobs rules; Section 8-10 lessons

qualitative_rules.rule: Part 5 (The Big Invite) names the same offer and participation action as Section 1. The assembled page contains no invented bonus, video button, guarantee, timer, audience-exclusion section, or testimonial block.
